ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-signing and continuous screening of all shareholders, directors, officers, ultimate beneficial owners and material counterparties against the EU Consolidated List of Financial Sanctions (UN-derived and autonomous EU regimes), the United Nations Security Council sanctions list, the Luxembourg national enforcement measures issued by the CSSF, and the domestic PEP definition under the Law of 12 November 2004 (persons entrusted with prominent public functions at national, EU or international level, their family members, and known close associates). In addition, because payments are routed through Stripe and Wise and may clear in USD, prudent screening against the OFAC SDN List and OFAC non-SDN consolidated lists shall be performed to mitigate secondary sanctions risk. Enhanced due diligence and denial-of-engagement protocol shall apply whenever a match cannot be affirmatively cleared, when source of funds cannot be documented, or when a sanctioned jurisdiction without lawful exemption is involved. Adverse-media screening and UBO re-verification are required at onboarding and at each material ownership or directorship change.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — official RCSL portal accessible at https://www.lbr.lu, operating the Registry of Commerce and Companies (RCSL) and the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutes and filings are made in one of the official administrative languages of Luxembourg (French, German or Luxembourgish); French is the primary registry practice language. Where the originating documentation or the company name is expressed in a non-Latin script, a Latin-alphabet transliteration is mandatory. The corporate name must not be misleading, contrary to public policy, or likely to create confusion with existing registered entities. For a Société à Responsabilité Limitée, the name must terminate with the descriptor 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or the abbreviation 'SARL' / 'S.à r.l.'.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Banking terms (prior authorisation of the CSSF mandatory)
Assurance / Réassurance / Mutuelle (prior authorisation of the Commissariat aux Assurances mandatory)
Fonds d'investissement / FCP / SICAV / SICAF (prior CSSF authorisation mandatory)
Bourse / Trading venue / Clearing (prior Ministry of Finance and regulatory authorisation mandatory)
Avocat (prior admission and authorisation of the Ordre des Avocats du Barreau de Luxembourg mandatory)
Notaire / Huissier de justice (prior authorisation of the Chambre des Notaires / ministerial approval mandatory)
Auditeur / Expert-comptable (prior authorisation of the Institut des Réviseurs d'Entreprises mandatory)
Loterie / Casino / Gambling (prior authorisation of the Ministry of Justice and the Gambling Authority mandatory)
État / Communal / Municipal / Luxembourg (any use falsely suggesting affiliation with the Grand Duchy, the State, or a public-law body is prohibited)
Hôpital / Clinique / Pharmaceutical terms (prior authorisation of the Ministry of Health mandatory)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The name reservation may be extended through the LBR online account for successive one-month periods, subject to payment of the applicable LBR fee and confirmation that no conflicting registration has intervened. Upon rejection, the applicant shall file a written administrative reconsideration request with the RCSL within 15 days of the refusal notification, annexing the name-clearance certificate, the proposed name, and reasoned argument that the name satisfies the conditions of the Law of 19 December 2002. If the registrar affirms the refusal, the applicant may bring judicial proceedings before the Tribunal d'Arrondissement de Luxembourg (Civil or Commercial Chamber) within 40 days of notification of the affirmed refusal, seeking an order compelling registration or annulling the registrar's decision, in accordance with the Law of 19 December 2002 and the New Code of Civil Procedure. A rejected or expired name may also be re-filed with a corrected or amended distinctive element.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permitted. Luxembourg requires every SARL to maintain a statutory registered office (siège social) situated in the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, in accordance with the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies. The Law of 31 May 1999 on the domiciliation of commercial companies permits a licensed professional domiciliation agent to provide the registered address. A pure virtual mailbox without local correspondence handling is not acceptable; the domiciliation agent must be able to receive court summons, official notifications, tax correspondence and banking correspondence. For a non-regulated, low-risk online subtitle and AI dubbing studio, such an arrangement is legally viable, provided the company maintains sufficient economic substance, local management presence and administrative capacity to satisfy Luxembourg anti-BEPS substance expectations and VAT registration requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low — estimated probability below 2% per annum of an unannounced physical on-site inspection for a non-regulated territorial post-production service entity. The authorities (RCSL, Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA, and the Joint Social Security Centre) conduct principally desk-based verification; physical presence may nevertheless be tested in the context of VAT desk audits, substance letters, or social-security contribution reviews, and the domiciliation agent must be able to evidence the company's access to the registered office upon request.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 710-1 et seq. governing the Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL), together with Articles 8, 9, and 24 on capital, formation formalities, and publication in the RESA.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), 12 rue Erasme, L-1468 Luxembourg; electronic filing through the eJustice portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) filed electronically by the Luxembourg notary via eJustice for RCS registration and publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The SARL must have a fully subscribed minimum share capital of EUR 12,000. At least 25% of the nominal value of each cash share must be paid up before notarial execution. The cash contributions must be deposited in a blocked escrow account opened in the company's formation name at a Luxembourg credit institution, and the bank's blockage certificate is released only after RCS registration. Contributions in kind must be fully vested and are subject to statutory auditor valuation if required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: At the constituent general meeting held on [Date] at the proposed registered office, the subscribers of all issued shares resolve as follows. First: that the share subscriptions and payments for the SARL's registered capital of EUR 12,000 (twelve thousand euros), divided into 12,000 ordinary shares of EUR 1.00 each, are approved and fully subscribed in accordance with the articles. Second: that the registered office of the company is adopted at [Address], L-1234 Luxembourg. Third: that [Name] is appointed sole manager (gérant), with authority to open bank accounts, execute the notarial deed, and make all statutory filings. Fourth: that the manager is directed to obtain VAT and social security registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name availability and corporate object verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS/LBR) through the eJustice portal and the Luxembourg notary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The proposed corporate name and business purpose are pre-vetted by the notary to ensure no identical or misleadingly similar name exists in the RCS. The corporate object is drafted to include automated subtitle transcription, dubbing, AI voice synthesis, audiovisual post-production, and related IT services under ISIC 5912 / NAICS 512191. A negative certificate or non-registration statement is obtained where available.
required_dossiers: Legal form statement (Société à Responsabilité Limitée)
Business activity description in French or English
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as identical or confusing, propose a revised distinctive name and resubmit through the notary; LBR does not require payment of any additional name reservation fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of notarial draft articles and constitutive documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (Chambre des Notaires du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary drafts the articles of association and capital plan. The draft fixes the corporate object, registered office, capital structure, duration, and management powers. Shareholders review the draft, confirm their subscription amounts, and approve the final text before execution.
required_dossiers: Business plan for post-production and AI subtitling services
Shareholder identification and beneficial ownership declarations
Power of attorney forms, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the LBR vetting process or the notary flags the corporate object as impermissibly broad, the object clause is narrowed to exclude regulated financial or broadcasting activities and the revised draft is resubmitted before execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of blocked share capital account and capital deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution subject to CSSF supervision; the notary supervises the blocking instruction.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked deposit account in the name of the SARL en formation at a Luxembourg bank. Deposit the required cash contribution, being at least 25% of each share's face value, toward the EUR 12,000 subscribed capital. The bank issues a blocking certificate addressed to the notary; funds are released only after the company obtains RCS registration.
required_dossiers: Bank instruction letter from the notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries KYC documentation, provide certified passports, tax residence certificates, and source-of-funds explanations. If the bank declines the account, open the blocked account at another Luxembourg credit institution or an EU credit institution acceptable to the notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All subscribers appear before the notary, personally or through a sworn power of attorney. The notary reads the final articles, confirms the capital subscriptions and payments, records the adoption of the registered office, and receives the appointment of the manager. The deed is signed by all parties and authenticated by the notary.
required_dossiers: Original power of attorney, if relevant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a subscriber is unavailable for signature, the notary postpones execution or accepts a certified original power of attorney. If the deed contains typographical defects, the notary prepares a correcting addendum or, if necessary, a re-execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés) through the eJustice portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within eight days after execution, the notary files the notarial deed, bank certificate, and registration application with the RCS. The RCS verifies legal conformity, allocates the registration number, and publishes the incorporation in the RESA electronic compendium. Legal personality commences upon registration and publication.
required_dossiers: Payment confirmation of RCS filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query or refuses registration, the notary files an explanatory memorandum or corrected deed within the fixed deadline. Legal personality remains suspended until the registration is admitted; the company may not transact binding business before admission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: VAT, corporate tax, employer, and occupational safety registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); commune for municipal permits; Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, apply through guichet.lu for VAT identification, corporate income tax registration, and municipal business tax registration. If staff will be hired, register with the CCSS as an employer. For the studio premises, obtain an office occupancy permit, fire safety confirmation, and submit the initial workplace risk assessment to the ITM.
required_dossiers: Signed lease or ownership proof for registered office and studio
Fire safety certificate and building occupancy permit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEDT delays issuance of the VAT number, provide the RCS extract and a certified translation of the statutes to prove taxpayer identity. If CCSS onboarding is delayed, contact CCSS with the RCS number and apply for retroactive enrollment within the legally permitted grace period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - the Ministry of Economy (Direction générale de l'industrie) is engaged only for classified industrial establishments; an AI subtitle transcription and voice production studio is a non-industrial service activity.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial operating license is required. The activity is not a classified establishment under the Luxembourg classified establishments regime and does not require a sectoral manufacturing permit.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - the activity falls outside Annex I and Annex II project categories of the amended Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment. No full EIA report or registered environmental permit is triggered by a studio-based post-production service.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC, or stack emission thresholds apply. Any HVAC or cooling equipment using F-gases must comply with Regulation (EU) No 517/2014 on fluorinated greenhouse gases. Kitchenette and sanitary wastewater must discharge to the public sanitary sewer in accordance with the applicable communal drainage regulation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The studio and office premises must obtain fire safety approval from the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS), a building occupancy permit from the competent commune, and workplace safety documentation filed with the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM). Employer affiliation with an approved occupational health service is compulsory once staff are hired.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) — Luxembourg Direct Tax Authority, 4 rue de la Congrégation, L-1352 Luxembourg — for corporate income tax, net wealth tax, withholding tax and transfer pricing; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT), 1-3 avenue Guillaume, L-1651 Luxembourg — for Value Added Tax (TVA) and registration duties; Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — for commercial (R.C.S.) registration and the national identification number; single digital filing gateway: MyGuichet.lu (business eSpace), supplemented by the eCDF electronic tax-filing module of the ACD/AEDT.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 — Incorporate the SARL by notarial deed and file the incorporation with the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) through MyGuichet/eJustice; the LBR automatically assigns an 11-digit national business registration number (matricule / numéro d'identification national), which serves as the master tax identity before the ACD. Step 2 — No separate direct-tax registration is required for a resident SARL: the ACD uses the matricule for all corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax assessments; annual returns are filed electronically through the MyGuichet/eCDF platform. Step 3 — Obtain the VAT ID by filing Form 640 (Déclaration pour assujettissement à la TVA) with the AEDT; resident SARLs receive a VAT identification number of the format LU + 8 digits with a modulo-97 checksum; registration is due before the first taxable supply and, for a resident SARL, no turnover de-minimis applies unless the small-enterprise franchise under Article 57 of the 1979 VAT Law is claimed. Step 4 — For a non-resident foreign entity without a Luxembourg establishment, registration with the AEDT via Form 640 is required when the entity makes taxable supplies in Luxembourg (e.g., intra-EU distance sales, B2B services subject to Luxembourg reverse-charge rules, or supplies of e-services to Luxembourg consumers above the OSS threshold); a non-EU applicant must normally appoint a Luxembourg VAT representative; the AEDT then issues a stand-alone Luxembourg VAT ID without an RCS number. Step 5 — Register as an employer with the Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS) if staff are engaged, and open the ACD e-filing account to receive pre-printed returns, notices and VAT statements; registration is processed typically within 5–15 business days where the file is complete.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: the Luxembourg SARL is an opaque, fully tax-resident corporation under Article 159 LIR and is subject to unlimited worldwide tax liability, with the only territorial carve-out being treaty-based exemption for profits attributable to a foreign permanent establishment. The standard Luxembourg corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités, IRC) is 15% on the first €175,000 of taxable profit and 17% on taxable profit above €175,000, plus a 7% employment solidarity surcharge calculated on the IRC, plus municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal) of 6.75% in Luxembourg City, resulting in an aggregate headline effective rate of approximately 24.94% on profits above €175,000. The SARL is also liable to a minimum annual net wealth tax (impôt sur la fortune) of €3,500, increased to €4,815 when the balance-sheet total exceeds €350 million. Profit is taxed on accrual, not distribution: dividends declared by the SARL are subject to a 15% Luxembourg withholding tax, reducible to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or the domestic participation exemption when the 10% shareholding/e1.2m acquisition-cost and 12-month holding tests are met. The SARL is therefore not a pass-through, hybrid or disregarded entity for Luxembourg tax purposes; the tax classification is mandatory and not elective, and non-resident ownership of the SARL does not alter its status.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Check-the-box and similar pass-through elections do not exist in Luxembourg's civil-law unitary tax system; the SARL is mandatorily taxed at entity level. Available statutory elections: (1) VAT group election under Article 60 of the 1979 VAT Law — resident entities with economic, financial and organisational links may apply to be treated as a single taxable person (assujetti unique) with joint and several liability, allowing consolidated intra-group VAT invoices; (2) Fiscal unity for direct tax under Article 164bis LIR — a Luxembourg-resident parent holding directly or indirectly at least 95% of a Luxembourg subsidiary may elect full absorption of the subsidiary's taxable results from the first tax year of the election; (3) Participation-exemption election for qualifying dividends and capital gains under Articles 166 and 168 LIR, requiring a durable 10% shareholding or an acquisition cost of at least €1.2 million and a 12-month holding period measured at the relevant assessment date; (4) Option to waive the small-business VAT franchise (Article 57 VAT Law) in order to charge VAT and recover input VAT; (5) OSS (One-Stop-Shop) election for intra-EU B2C distance sales and telecommunications/broadcasting/e-services, filed electronically through MyGuichet; (6) hybrid-mismatch elections are not available: the Law of 23 December 2016 implementing EU ATAD/ATAD2 imposes mandatory anti-hybrid adjustments, and a Luxembourg SARL cannot elect to be disregarded, transparent or treated as a branch of its shareholder; (7) where applicable, the EU cross-border loss-relief election and the arm's-length advance pricing agreement route are available with the ACD.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA) — Luxembourg VAT — governed by the amended Law of 12 February 1979 (Loi TVA), implementing Council Directive 2006/112/EC, and administered by the Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); all declarations and payments are made electronically via the MyGuichet/eCDF platform.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Domestic small-enterprise franchise threshold: €35,000 (EUR) of annual taxable turnover excluding VAT, under Article 57 of the 1979 VAT Law, below which a Luxembourg-established business may be exempt from VAT; above this threshold mandatory registration applies unless the exemption is waived. Intra-EU B2C distance-selling and digital e-services threshold: €10,000 (EUR) of cumulative annual European turnover for distance sales of goods and supplies of telecommunications, broadcasting and electronic services by a Luxembourg supplier; below €10,000 Luxembourg VAT is chargeable, at or above €10,000 the supply is taxed in the consumer's member state and the OSS return mechanism must be used. Non-established foreign suppliers: no registration threshold applies and a Luxembourg VAT ID is required from the first euro of Luxembourg-taxable supply, except for supplies covered by the €10,000 OSS regime or by the reverse-charge mechanism; intra-EU goods distance sales by non-established EU suppliers are each governed by the national €10,000 OSS ceiling as implemented in their own state. VAT registration is compulsory, not discretionary, when any threshold is exceeded, and VAT must be accounted for from the date the threshold is crossed.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg has not introduced real-time continuous transaction controls: there is no mandatory fiscal-clearance API, no government digital stamping, and no BTC/B2B e-invoicing mandate for private-sector invoices. B2G electronic invoicing to central, regional and municipal authorities is mandatory through the PEPPOL network in the EN 16931 data model pursuant to Luxembourg's transposition of Directive 2014/55/EU, with phased enforcement against suppliers to the national administration. B2B e-invoicing remains voluntary and contractually driven, although structured electronic invoices (EDI, PEPPOL, Factur-X) are accepted. All VAT periodical returns (monthly or quarterly depending on prior-year turnover), recapitulative statements (EC sales lists), Intrastat declarations and requested Luxembourg SAF-T standard audit files must be submitted electronically through MyGuichet/eCDF; the VAT books and source evidence must be retained for at least 10 years. The payment rails identified (Stripe, Wise) operate solely as payment service providers: they are not deemed suppliers, not electronic-interface marketplaces under the VAT e-commerce package, and do not trigger a VAT collection, OSS or deemed-supply obligation for the SARL beyond the obligation to invoice and account for the underlying supply.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (exemption with credit for input VAT) applies to: (a) exports of goods physically dispatched or transported out of the European Union by the supplier or on its behalf (Article 156(1)(b) of the 1979 VAT Law), subject to proof of removal; (b) intra-EU supplies of goods to a customer holding a valid VAT identification number in another member state, subject to VIES validation, EC sales list reporting and invoice references to the customer's EU VAT ID; (c) supplies of services directly connected with exported goods, such as transport, handling and ancillary services physically performed in Luxembourg in relation to goods leaving the EU; and (d) supplies placed under customs warehousing, inward processing or similar customs regimes. For the SARL's business of automated subtitle transcription, AI voice cloning and post-production dubbing, the normal outcome is territoriality rather than a classical zero rate: B2B supplies of such services to a customer established in another member state are taxable in the customer's state under the reverse charge (no Luxembourg VAT), and B2B supplies to a customer outside the EU are outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT; B2C supplies of e-services to EU consumers below the €10,000 threshold bear Luxembourg VAT, above the threshold they are taxed at destination via OSS, and B2C supplies to non-EU consumers fall outside Luxembourg VAT. The SARL retains the right to deduct input VAT attributable to these export-like supplies, and a non-EU-established customer may recover improperly incurred Luxembourg VAT through the 13th Directive procedure before the AEDT.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/EAS) accepted by Luxembourg Customs evidencing the physical departure of goods from EU territory
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, CMR consignment note or equivalent third-party transport document proving removal and transport route
Commercial invoice and purchase order identifying the buyer, description of goods or services, quantities, prices and Incoterms
VIES validation output or certified copy of the customer's EU VAT identification number for intra-EU zero-rating
EC Sales List (recapitulative statement) filing acknowledgement and Intrastat declarations where goods movement thresholds apply
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT/Stripe/Wise payment-rail settlement confirmation evidencing receipt of export proceeds and foreign-currency conversion

Executed service agreement, delivery certificates (e.g., subtitle master files, AI voice-clone audio deliverables), usage and distribution licence documentation, and technical acceptance reports for A/V post-production services
13th Directive VAT refund application file submitted to the AEDT where Luxembourg VAT has been charged to a non-EU-established client, together with the AEDT decision or refund receipt
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg domestic law imposes no exchange-control or mandatory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline; the 180-day standard recorded in this field serves as the administrative benchmark for export-proceed substantiation, transfer-pricing documentation and ACD risk review. The AEDT and ACD enjoy a general audit window of five years from the end of the relevant assessment year, extended without limit in cases of fraud, wilful default or failure to file. Where zero-rating or export exemption is claimed without the required customs, transport, VIES or payment evidence, the administration clawbacks VAT at the standard rate of 17% (or at the applicable reduced rate) on the full supply value, together with statutory default interest, a late-payment surcharge of 10% and administrative fines of up to €25,000 per adjustment; criminal tax-fraud proceedings may additionally result in imprisonment of up to five years and further judicial fines. On the direct-tax side, the ACD may recharacterise funds or receivables that have not been repatriated or economically justified as hidden dividend distributions or disguised profit distributions under Article 56 LIR and the ATAD general anti-abuse rule, triggering reassessment of corporate income tax, municipal business tax, a 15% dividend withholding tax, interest and penalties. To mitigate audit exposure, the SARL should maintain a per-transaction export evidence file, including customs declarations, transport documents, VIES screenshots, contracts, delivery certificates, licence confirmations and bank/remittance records, retained for at least ten years and reconciled to the VAT return, EC sales list and annual accounts.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque Centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) is the national central bank and Luxembourg's monetary and balance-of-payments authority; the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) is the integrated financial sector supervisor competent for banking, AML/CFT supervision, and payment/e-money institution oversight. There is no separate exchange-control administration; the BCL operates within the Eurosystem and the CSSF enforces prudential and AML rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg maintains full current-account and capital-account liberalisation under Articles 63-66 TFEU, the OECD Capital Movements Code, and the application of the euro as legal tender. There are no exchange-control approvals, no FDI licensing requirements for post-production subtitle and AI voice-cloning services, and no prohibition on inward capital or outward profit remittance. Dividends and profit shares may be freely transferred in EUR or convertible foreign currency once corporate law distribution tests are met and the paying agent's AML/KYC obligations are satisfied. The only material obstacles are tax-driven, not FX-driven: a Luxembourg Sàrl distributing dividends is normally subject to Luxembourg withholding tax of 15% (subject to treaty reductions or the Parent-Subsidiary Directive where applicable), and shareholders' loan repayments must comply with thin-capitalisation and transfer-pricing rules. Inconvertibility risk is negligible because EUR is freely traded and the BCL has never imposed surrender or rationing measures.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio apply in Luxembourg. Export proceeds derived from subtitling, dubbing, and AI transcription services may be retained in any foreign currency in bank accounts without compulsory sale, surrender, or BCL authorisation. Banks acting as reporting agents must provide transaction-level balance-of-payments statistics to the BCL for eligible cross-border payments, typically above the EUR 12,500 reporting threshold, and the SARL must preserve underlying invoices, contracts, and transaction narratives for at least five years. These obligations are statistical and AML/CFT-based, not exchange-control restrictions.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium-High for inbound collection and subcontractor payout routing; Low as a substitute for a licensed credit institution or statutory share-capital escrow. A Luxembourg-authorised payment institution or e-money institution supervised by the CSSF may hold payment or electronic-money accounts but may not take deposits or create bank credit. International EMIs such as Wise and Stripe may be used as regulated settlement/technical payment processors for trade receivables if the serving entity is authorised or passported in the EEA under PSD2 and subject to safeguarding rules. However, the civil-law formation procedure of a Luxembourg Sàrl requires the paid-up share capital to be indefeasibly evidenced, typically through a blocked account in the name of the company at a Luxembourg/EU credit institution certified to the notary; a pure EMI balance cannot satisfy that formal proof. Offshore digital EMIs without passporting, deposit-taking capability, or a local AML nexus create a legal concentration risk and should not be treasury counterparties for material balances.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg company law requires an authentic notarial deed, meaning the Sàrl's founder and any appointed manager generally appear before a Luxembourg notary, either physically or via secure electronic notarisation where permitted, and the notary must verify identity and capacity. For banking KYC, CSSF-compliant remote onboarding is permitted, including qualified electronic identification and video verification, but most tier-1 banks will still require a physical interview for at least one managing director, ultimate beneficial owner, or a locally designated authorised signatory, particularly for non-resident directors and companies without an existing Luxembourg banking relationship. For an AI post-production SARL with directors outside the jurisdiction, the recommended compliance posture is to schedule an in-person KYC meeting in Luxembourg, or to grant a local manager a notarised and apostilled power of attorney with signature specimen, document originals, and corroborated source of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated Sàrl with non-resident director and no demonstrated local economic substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered lease or commercial sub-lease agreement; utility invoice and internet/telephony service contract in the company's name; local substance description including Luxembourg-based manager, service agreements, accounting firm relationship, payroll or corporate tax filings; organisational chart identifying management and employees; signed board resolution approving account opening and treasury mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: AI voice-cloning, subtitling, and post-production business classified as intellectual-property-centric digital activity with cross-border revenue flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Portfolio of binding client contracts and purchase orders; detailed workflow description distinguishing AI-generated transcription, human post-editing, and localisation; IP ownership or licensing chain, including copyright registrations and assignment deeds; software and data licences; data-processing agreements and GDPR or DPIA documentation evidencing lawful handling of actor and author data; projected transaction flows with counterparty jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent outbound payments through Stripe, Wise, or similar payment aggregators to numerous subcontractors and voice studios in multiple countries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Whitelist of subcontractors with full legal names, registration numbers, and address verification; master subcontracting agreements and per-project statements of work; invoice integrity tracking and PO-to-invoice-to-payment reconciliation; sanctions and PEP screening results for each counterparty; explanations for any unusual or split payments; confirmation that all funds are settled through EEA-regulated institutions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner located in, or nationality aligned with, a FATF-high-risk monitoring jurisdiction or a jurisdiction requiring enhanced due diligence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport copy and proof of residential tax residence; sworn declaration of legitimate wealth and source of funds; audited or bank-supported evidence for the capital injection; curriculum vitae and business substance narrative; corporate registers and ownership chain documentation demonstrating transparency; consent to enhanced monitoring and periodic Source-of-Funds/Wealth re-verification.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For the SARL's paid-up share capital, the inward transfer must be executed before notarisation to a blocked escrow account in the company's name at a Luxembourg/EU credit institution. If the transfer is in EUR within the euro area, use a SEPA Credit Transfer (ISO 20022 pain.001) with the remittance narrative "Capital subscription - Société à Responsabilité Limitée en formation"; if in USD or other foreign currency, use SWIFT MT103 with a corresponding-bank clearing path and the balance-of-payments flag for direct investment equity capital. The bank must provide a blocked-funds certificate or irrevocable confirmation used by the Luxembourg notary to authenticate payment of the statutory minimum capital. After registration, the funds are released to the operational account on the company's instruction. For subsequent intra-group debt or equity injections from a foreign parent, use SWIFT MT103 or SEPA SCT with the appropriate balance-of-payments category and ensure invoices, shareholder resolutions, and intercompany loan agreements are retained to demonstrate commercial purpose and financing substance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For subcontractor payments, royalty remittances, AI platform licensing fees, and operating expenses, the primary clearing rails are SEPA SCT for EUR payments within the EEA, SWIFT MT103 for cross-border USD or non-EEA payments, and SWIFT MT202/COV for correspondent-bank settlement where required by the receiving institution. Trade-related documentary settlement is generally unnecessary for intangibles and services, but where the counterparty requires assurance for high-value technology or post-production deliverables, a standard commercial letter of credit may be issued through SWIFT MT700/MT707; in the digital services context, bank-guaranteed payment undertakings and standby LCs are more practical. Export proceeds may also be collected through Stripe or Wise rails, provided settled funds are swept daily to the primary Luxembourg operating account at a tier-1 bank to avoid concentration risk and to maintain a clean audit trail for tax and AML purposes.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD) for matched intercompany funding and cash-flow hedging
EUR/USD non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed exclusively with an EU-authorised credit institution or MiFID-qualified counterparty, subject to EMIR clearing, margin, and reporting obligations
Short-date EUR/foreign-currency FX spot trades supporting operational cash-flow conversion

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (annual accounts and management report) approved by the general meeting and filed with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within eight months after the financial year-end balance sheet date (e.g., by 31 August for a Calendar Year entity with a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing exposes directors/managers to criminal fines up to EUR 25,000 and/or administrative coercive fines; failure to file annual accounts for three consecutive financial years allows the RCS to initiate administrative strike-off (radiation) after formal notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owner information on the Luxembourg UBO register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually during the calendar month immediately preceding the anniversary of the initial UBO declaration; interim updates must be filed within 15 days of a qualifying shareholding change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-disclosure or inaccurate confirmation is punishable by criminal fines of EUR 750 to EUR 25,000 and possible imprisonment; shareholders in breach may have voting rights suspended and persistent non-compliance exposes the entity to administrative penalties and strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Luxembourg SARL must appoint an approved statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises) if, for two consecutive financial years, it exceeds at least two of the following thresholds: total balance sheet EUR 4,400,000; net turnover EUR 8,800,000; average workforce 50 employees. A shareholder or group of shareholders holding at least 10% of the capital may also trigger a mandatory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP as codified by the Law of 19 April 2014 on commercial companies and the Grand-Ducal accounting regulations; IFRS as adopted by the EU may be used for consolidated accounts and, subject to election, for individual annual accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each year the SARL must file an electronic confirmation on the RBE portal during the month preceding the anniversary of the initial UBO declaration, attesting that the beneficial ownership data are complete and accurate. Any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be reported to the RBE within 15 days of the company gaining knowledge thereof; the annual confirmation must reflect all interim updates and the then-current shareholding structure.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500 – USD 4,000 per annum for a standard registered office / domiciliation agent service in Luxembourg City
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 – USD 20,000 per annum for a certified audit of a typical SARL preparing Luxembourg GAAP annual accounts

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% combined (Luxembourg City: 17.00% CIT + 1.19% solidarity surcharge on CIT + 6.75% municipal business tax); municipal rate varies by commune (typically 6.75%-10.50%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holidays. Targeted preferences: 80% exemption on qualifying IP income (effective combined rate on IP income approx. 5.04%); 100% participation exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains; notional interest deduction on increased equity; R&D tax credit (44% of eligible R&D expenses up to EUR 1m, 50% on EUR 1m-2m tranche, 6% on excess); investment tax credit; EUR 500,000 net wealth tax exemption for small companies; unlimited loss carryforward with annual cap.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no time limit for losses incurred from 2017; 10-year limit for pre-2017 losses; utilization capped annually at EUR 50,000 plus 50% of taxable income exceeding EUR 50,000)
